findings.trigger_condition: Edge stream contains two nodes A and B where A == B is True but one is hashable (e.g., frozenset({1,2}), int, custom hashable with __hash__) and the other is unhashable (e.g., set({1,2}), list, custom object with __hash__=None and __eq__ returning True). Canonical example is set vs frozenset equality or HashableNode('same') vs UnhashableNode('same') where __eq__ compares .value.
findings.root_cause: _id_of splits identity resolution into two disjoint registries and never cross-compares them. The try-branch (lines 42, 53-56) indexes only hash_buckets dict for hashable values, while the except TypeError branch (lines 44-52) linear-scans only unhashable_ids/unhashable_nodes. Neither branch probes the other registry for an equal object, so equal values separated by hashability receive distinct integer IDs.
findings.impact: Node deduplication, indegree accounting, edge deduplication (seen_edges uses IDs), and cycle detection all operate on IDs, so the graph is corrupted: the same logical node appears as two distinct nodes in output layers (e.g., [['root'], [hashable, unhashable]] instead of [['root'], [first]]), layer counts are inflated, repeated edges are not deduplicated, and self-loop or directed cycles formed solely by cross-hashability equal nodes (e.g., dependency_layers([(first, equal_unhashable)])) are not recognized as cycles and fail to raise DependencyCycleError.
findings.suggested_validation: Run supplemental cross_hashability check: class HashableNode with __hash__=hash(value) and __eq__ on .value, class UnhashableNode with __hash__=None and same __eq__; first=HashableNode('same'), equal_unhashable=UnhashableNode('same'); result=dependency_layers([(first,'root'),(equal_unhashable,'root')]); assert result==[['root'],[first]] and result[1][0] is first; observed is [['root'],[first, equal_unhashable]]. Also test self-loop dependency_layers([(first, equal_unhashable)]) - expected DependencyCycleError but returns [[unhashable],[hashable]] with two layers.

findings.trigger_condition: Edge stream contains many distinct unhashable nodes, e.g., N distinct list/dict objects or custom unhashable instances such as [([i+1],[i]) for i in range(N)] or [({'id':i+1},{'id':i}) for i in range(N)] with N>=2000.
findings.root_cause: In the except TypeError path _id_of performs a linear scan 'for idx, candidate in zip(unhashable_ids, unhashable_nodes): if candidate is value or candidate == value' over all previously registered unhashable nodes (lines 44-45). No hash acceleration, index, or bucketing is used; every new distinct unhashable node pays O(U) where U is current unhashable count. Hashable collision bucket scan on line 53 is per-bucket but unhashable scan is global.
findings.impact: Total time for N distinct unhashable nodes is O(N^2) equality comparisons. Verified: N=2000 list chain ~0.16s, N=4000 ~0.65s (3.9x for 2x input, quadratic) vs hashable tuple chain N=4000 ~0.004s (linear). Very deep acyclic inputs that the spec requires to handle without recursion become quadratically slow and can time out or exhaust CPU, violating resource/complexity expectations distinct from recursion depth.
findings.suggested_validation: Benchmark dependency_layers([([i+1],[i]) for i in range(N)]) for N=2000 vs N=4000 and measure wall-time ratio ~4x (quadratic) rather than ~2x (linear); profile with cProfile and observe hotspot in _id_of lines 44-45. Compare against hashable equivalent [((i+1,), (i,)) for i in range(N)] which scales linearly and completes in milliseconds.
